newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tyndall to buy Oceanic for A$40 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tyndall to buy Oceanic for A$40 mln.

text.p: Tyndall Australia Ltd said on Thursday it had agreed in principle to purchase Oceanic Capital Holdings Ltd for A$40 million.
The company said Oceanic was involved in life insurance and funds management in Australia and New Zealand, with operations conducted through its Oceanic Life Ltd unit.

Tyndall said Oceanic was owned by Financial Insurance Fund L.P., a United States-based group of insurers and reinsurers, which owned the company for five years after purchasing it from the debt-ridden State Bank of South Australia.
It said Oceanic had funds under management of A$250 million, bringing Tyndall's total funds under management of A$6.3 billion. Oceanic has 160,000 policyholders in Australia and New Zealand.
Tyndall, which is 51 percent owned by Guinness Peat Group Plc, said the purchase price would include a mixture of cash and the issue of medium term convertible debt.

"This (the Oceanic purchase) doesn't diminish our chances of further acquisitions," Tyndall managing director Michael Wilkins told a news conference. "We have a parent whose philosophy is to grow through acquisitions," Wilkins said.

Tyndall shares were two cents higher at A$1.98 at 12.05 p.m. (0205 GMT). The company told the Australian Stock Exchange on Tuesday in response to a query about the rise in its share price that it was in acquisition talks and planned an announcement on Thursday. At the time, Tyndall shares had risen to A$2.00 from A$1.65 on October 15.
